title: Acknowledge HMI fault at the hospital area and retry operation
summary: Source-specific incident recovery for an HMI fault reported at the hospital area within the UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH) incident context. The evidence supports viewing the faulted HMI, not unplugging the HMI, using the on-screen acknowledge action, retrying, confirming whether the tote is ID 28, and validating that the condition is cleared and reported as all good.
when_to_use: Use when the HMI associated with the hospital area is reported as showing a fault in the UPS Haslet TX (TXRTH) incident context, and the source-supported response is to acknowledge the fault on the HMI and retry the operation without unplugging the HMI.
not_for: Do not use this runbook as justification to unplug the HMI; the source explicitly says not to unplug it.
Do not use this runbook for HMI project updates, stuck-task recovery creation, or undocumented task-debug procedures; those were discussed later in the incident but not performed as this recovery.
Do not use this runbook when the faulted device or tote context cannot be matched to the hospital-area HMI evidence in this case.

roles_and_responsibilities.responsibility: Guide the acknowledge-and-retry recovery, confirm the tote ID requested in the support exchange, and validate whether the condition clears.
Access or view the HMI at the hospital area, perform the on-screen acknowledge action when directed, retry, and report the tote ID and recovery status.

safety_notes: Do not unplug the HMI during this procedure; the source-supported response explicitly rejected unplugging.
Use only the on-screen acknowledge-and-retry action supported by the incident evidence.
Do not perform undocumented HMI changes or recovery modifications based on this case alone.

steps.title: Keep the HMI connected

steps.failure_condition: The next intended action is to unplug the HMI or otherwise remove it from service without source support.

steps.title: Acknowledge the fault and retry
steps.purpose: Apply the exact recovery action supported by the incident evidence.
steps.instruction: Use the HMI acknowledge control, then try the operation again.
steps.expected_result: The fault is acknowledged and the operation is retried without unplugging the HMI.
steps.healthy_condition: The HMI accepts the acknowledge action and the retry proceeds.
steps.failure_condition: The HMI does not allow acknowledge, the retry cannot be attempted, or the fault remains after retry.

success_criteria: The hospital-area HMI fault is acknowledged without unplugging the HMI.
The tote involved is confirmed as ID 28.
The site reports the condition is all good.
healthy_conditions: The HMI remains connected throughout the procedure.
The acknowledge action is available and accepted on the HMI.
The tote at the hospital is confirmed as 28.
The post-retry status is reported as all good.
failure_conditions: The HMI cannot be accessed or the fault cannot be confirmed.
The only contemplated next step is unplugging the HMI.
Acknowledge-and-retry does not clear the fault.
The tote ID cannot be confirmed.
The site does not confirm that the condition is all good after retry.
escalation_guidance: Escalate if acknowledge-and-retry does not clear the fault or the HMI still shows the issue after retry.
Escalate if the HMI cannot remain connected or cannot be operated using the acknowledge control.
Escalate if the tote ID or recovery status cannot be confirmed in the hospital-area context.
Do not proceed into HMI update work, stuck-task recovery changes, or other undocumented remediation based on this runbook alone.
